Definition: used only in plural the intestines, or (collectively) the abdomen, figuratively, sympathy; by implication, a vest; by extension the stomach, the uterus (or of men, the seat of generation), the heart (figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: The bowels are the inward parts, and the Bible makes them the seat of the deepest feelings: God promises Abraham a son who will come out of his own bowels, Jeremiah says his bowels are troubled for Ephraim, and Jonah prays from the fish's belly. The psalm says God's law is within the heart, and God promises David a son out of his bowels to sit on his throne.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bowels are the Bible's word for the place where love hurts: God says His bowels are troubled for His people, and that is not sentiment but the heart of the Father. When the law is within us, the same inward place holds both His word and His compassion.
